title: Adaptive reservation demuxer for init-gen scheduling: fairness vs latency control
creator: Priya Shah
description:
Context:
Redwood's serving runtime must balance two conflicting objectives across init-generation (init-gen) and streaming phases: predictable latency for interactive tenants and high aggregate throughput for batchy/low-priority tenants. Current monolithic admission logic couples reservation (how much slice to reserve for a request) with execution demultiplexing, which makes it hard to: 1) provide long-tail latency isolation, 2) apply kernel-selection hints independently, and 3) enforce per-tenant fairness when stages produce wildly different kernel costs (dense attention vs sparse attention).

Goal:
Design and implement an 'Adaptive Reservation Demuxer' that decouples reservation accounting from execution dispatch for init-gen and streaming generations. The demuxer will: 1) allocate lightweight reservations up-front (soft credits) based on tenant SLO, historical latency, and token-cost estimates; 2) perform an execution-time demultiplex step that rebalances slices across tenants using kernel hint signals (attention density, kv-cache hit, quantization level); and 3) expose a latency-vs-throughput dial controlled by per-route policy.

Proposed design (high level):
- Reservation layer: small, fast path that grants soft token/time credits derived from a tenant's SLO band and recent tail latency. Credits are intentionally conservative for low-latency tenants and generous for throughput-focused tenants.
- Execution demuxer: when GPU-ready, the demuxer collects in-flight slices and reassigns execution slots using kernel-cost hints and the remaining reservation budget. This reassign step can split a reservation (phase-split) into micro-slices if kernel-cost projections are high, or coalesce adjacent low-cost slices to improve GPU packing.
- Kernel hint integration: attention-density probe (lightweight estimator during prefill) and kv-cache-hit predictor inform kernel selection and micro-slice sizing. Demuxer uses these hints to pick optimized kernels and to decide on phase-splitting thresholds.
- Fairness model: two-tier fairness combining (a) long-term tenant credit replenishment (throughput fairness window) and (b) short-term latency headroom tokens to protect tenants with tight SLOs.
- Latency/throughput knob: per-route policy parameter 'latency_priority' ∈ [0..1]. 0 => maximize GPU packing/throughput, 1 => prioritize latency isolation (smaller reservations, hedging, early preemption).

Acceptance criteria / success metrics:
- Latency SLA adherence: 99th percentile init-gen latency for P0 tenants improves (or at least does not regress) compared to baseline under mixed workload with 10% P0 traffic and 90% throughput traffic. Target: <= baseline + 5% for P0, and throughput loss <= 12% overall.
- Fairness: over a 30-minute mixed-run, long-term weighted throughput per-tenant matches configured quotas within 8%.
- Kernel efficiency: proportion of calls using optimal kernel hints increases by at least 15% vs baseline sampling approach.
- Stability: no incident-level errors introduced in rollout canary (observability windows: latency, error-rate, GPU utilization).

Implementation plan (milestones):
1) Simulation & model (Week 1-2): implement a simulator that consumes traces and emulates reservations+demux decisions. Produce step-function models for token cost estimation.
2) Instrumentation & metrics (Week 2): add lightweight attention-density probe to prefill path; KV-hit predictor counters; expose new telemetry.
3) Demuxer prototype (Week 3-4): implement in runtime as opt-in scheduler flag. Start with deterministic micro-slicing and simple credit policy.
4) Kernel hint integration (Week 5): plumb kernel selection hints to runtime kernel selector and validate on small models.
5) Canary rollout (Week 6): route 5% of traffic for two tenants (one P0 interactive, one throughput-heavy) to demuxer; monitor.
6) Policy refinement & gradual rollout (Week 7-8): tune latency_priority defaults and credit replenishment curve.

Testing & validation:
- Trace-driven simulation using GH tracebank and synthetic spike tests (burst 10x).
- Local microbench harness with model-mock to validate kernel hinting decisions and micro-slice packing.
- Canary metrics: p50/p90/p99 latency, GPU occupancy, kernel switch count, kv-cache reuse rate, tenant throughput share.

Risk & mitigations:
- Risk: over-splitting causes GPU throughput collapse. Mitigation: set minimum micro-slice duration and coalesce low-cost adjacent slices in demuxer.
- Risk: inaccurate kernel hints lead to wrong kernel selection. Mitigation: conservative fallback to baseline kernels and continuous A/B of hint thresholds.
- Risk: billing and metering mismatch due to decoupled reservations. Mitigation: maintain accurate mapping from reservation to actual execution tokens and add reconciliation job.

Rollout plan:
- Feature gated (runtime flag) + per-customer opt-in in Dedicated/Private.
- Canary on hosted with two internal test tenants, then 5 external beta customers under SRE supervision.
- Phased ramp with automated rollback on SLO regressions.

Open questions (TBD):
- Exact credit replenishment curve parameters for steady-state fairness.
- How to combine quantization-level hints with attention-density for kernel selection.
- Accounting model for partially-executed reservations (preempted micro-slice).

Artifacts & links:
- Design doc (internal): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUN/Adaptive+Reservation+Demuxer
- Simulator code: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime-sim/tree/eng/adm-sim
- PR (initial demuxer): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1824
- Perf dashboard (canary): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/adm-canary/perf-overview

Next steps:
- Complete simulator runs with three production traces and post results (priority this sprint).
- Implement attention-density probe prototype and land metrics pre-submit.
